## What you should be able to do tonight

- Derive Itô's lemma from a blank page in under five minutes.
- State the quadratic variation identity and the three consequences that follow from it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>35 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Finish anything outstanding from days 239 to 244. The explicit Ornstein-Uhlenbeck solution is the one worth completing, because week 39's stochastic volatility models are built from it.
:::

<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Blank page, timed: the quadratic variation identity, the derivation of Itô's lemma, and the solution of geometric Brownian motion. ## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Arithmetic, timed, thirty-fifth sitting. Ten two-digit multiplications and the sevenths.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> A statistics question asked in exactly this form: you have two estimators of the same quantity, one unbiased with high variance and one biased with low variance. How do you choose? Answer with mean squared error and then say what changes if the estimate feeds a position size rather than a report.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> A coding question: implement a function that computes the running median of a stream in better than linear time per update. Two heaps is the answer; write it, then say the complexity of insert and of query.
:::
:::
